subtopic: API Rate Limiting (Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket)
question_text: In a distributed cluster of 20 API gateway instances, why is naive in-memory rate limiting inadequate?

options.text: In-memory rate limiters cannot track IP addresses
Requests are distributed across instances; an attacker could cycle requests across all 20 nodes, effectively multiplying their allowed threshold by 20x
Operating system memory leaks will occur on high traffic

answer_explanation: Without a centralized shared atomic state (e.g. Redis sliding window or token bucket via Lua scripts), independent node counters fail to enforce cluster-wide limits.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Without a centralized shared atomic state (e.g. Redis sliding window or token bucket via Lua scripts), independent node counters fail to enforce cluster-wide limits.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
